    @pytest.mark.priority(12)
    def test_validate_forceOpen_content1_from_userPortal(self):
        allure.dynamic.title(
        f"Given a course with force_open_content enabled, which has 1 chapter & 4 contents where FOC enabled for first3 contents, 1 releasing on day1 and rest on day8 of week1,"
        f"when user is on day4 of the program"
        f"then the user should see content1 as mandatory only"
    )
    
        _, auth_token = self.createSession(config.get_login_credentials()['FORCE_OPEN_PDF_UNAME'], config.get_login_credentials()['FORCE_OPEN_PDF_PWD'])
        assert auth_token is not None, "Failed to create session"
        url = f"{self.base_url}/api/v1/mandatory_content?date={datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d')}"
        headers = {
                "Authorization": "Token token="+auth_token,
                "Content-Type": "application/json"
            }
        response = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
        assert response.status_code == 200, "Expected status code 200 for fetching mandatory content"
        response_data = response.json()
        print("Mandatory content response data:", response_data)
        assert len(response_data) == 1, "Expected exactly one mandatory content item"
        docId_fromWeb = response_data[0]["document_id"]
        print("Document ID from web:", docId_fromWeb)
        print("Document ID from coach:", self.__class__.content_id)
        # assert docId_fromWeb != self.__class__.content_id, f"Expected document IDs to differ, but both are {docId_fromWeb}"
    
        #validate whether feature flag is enabled
        url = f"{self.base_url}/api/v1/mandatory_content/enabled"
        response = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
        assert response.status_code == 200, "Expected status code 200 for fetching user details"
        response_data = response.json()
        print("User details response data:", response_data)
        assert response_data["enabled"] is True, "Expected force_open_content feature flag to be True"
        # self.driver.find_element("xpath", "//a[text()='Accept']").click()
